post.summary: An admin (CLEARANCE_ADMINS), or a delegate naming one in the on-behalf-of header, opens a break-glass window on one protected environment: a reason, a TTL (a Go duration, at most CLEARANCE_BREAKGLASS_MAX_TTL, never over 4h) and the cluster and env. Recorded as breakglass.open and committed before the answer, so the record precedes every change it covers. It clears nothing; exceptions inside it carry its id. At the TTL the core reconciles it (breakglass.close).

post.summary: An admin closes a break-glass window early; it is reconciled at once (breakglass.close lists what the record store knows changed in the window).

get.summary: A change's state and its live clearance token (a DSSE envelope and its JWT projection; null when the change is not cleared, its token was revoked by a new head, or it lapsed). For a registered provider and the verifier that registered the change; people read changes through clearance-api. A token with less than half its life left is re-issued (same nonce) before it is returned.

post.summary: The outcome of a cleared terraform-plan change's apply, once, from the principal that registered the change: whether it ran, the sha256 of the plan file applied, the resources from the apply's JSON log, when it started and finished, and its error. Recorded as deploy.outcome with matched (verified: the applied digest is the cleared one); a mismatch is also a deploy.exception of kind digest-mismatch. A second outcome is DG-STATE.

get.summary: Long-poll a change: the same answer as getClearance, returned as soon as the change's state is not `state` (default: its state when the call arrived), or after `timeout` seconds (1 to 60, default 30) with changed false. For any subject kind; the same callers as getClearance. The core is the one writer, so it wakes the call on the write itself (an in-process notifier), never by polling the database.

put.summary: The provider's whole set of cluster-pinned agent definitions (its Agent XR loader's pins and rejections) replaces the set the core holds. The core decides each pin itself (schema, name, owner, workload identity, not a bundled name) and records each change once as definition.load, definition.unload or definition.reject; provenance then reads the pinned definitions. Only the provider registered with definitions: true.

post.summary: A person (an admin, CLEARANCE_ADMINS, or a delegate naming one in the on-behalf-of header) sets how an observed change ended: state (reverted, ratified, declared-break-glass, still-live) and, for reverted, its cause (agent-caused, policy-triggered, human-initiated, automated-remediation, requirement-changed, external-dependency, unattributed), with an optional note. Recorded as a resolution record about the observation, naming the person (principal, initiator, resolution.by). Append-only: an edit is another record about the same seq, and the newest wins when it is read; the earlier ones stay in the chain.
